statement: For every simply connected spherical domain with nondegenerate frontier, every orientation-preserving ambient homeomorphism fixing the complement pointwise fixes the prime-end circle pointwise. Actual prime-end extension gives a continuous injective homomorphism into the boundary-fixed disk homeomorphism group, with dense image and exact same-label operator conjugation. At every non-locally-connected frontier, a nontrivial impression supplies explicit shrinking supported maps proving failure of inverse continuity and one boundary-fixed disk map outside the image. The locally connected case is the topological isomorphism already proved in C68.
depends_on: Verified crosscut-chain compactification and neighborhood basis in Binder-Rojas-Yampolsky Section 3.1; exact spherical crosscut/access endpoint and radial landing facts in Ortega-Ruiz del Portal 2011, printed pages 1571-1572, 1575 and 1581; the unlinked-access Jordan proof, closed Polish graph/open-mapping argument, compact-support density, and nontrivial-impression constructions proved here; C30 Polish open orbit theorem; C68 locally connected comparison
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), actual prime-end and ambient relative centralizer comparisons.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. No continuous landing function on an arbitrary prime-end arc is assumed. The proof uses a smaller genuine crosscut neighborhood with closure inside that arc, and constructs the two-access Jordan curve explicitly. It retains the actual ambient and disk topologies, the original operator labels, and the restriction kernel.
computational_checks: This is a qualitative topological comparison, proved by explicit maps and inverse formulas. Its impression-based witnesses require no numerical approximation or finite quotient computation.
notes: The map is continuous and injective, not asserted to induce an injection on fundamental groups. For non-locally-connected frontier the proof establishes a dense proper image and discontinuity of the actual inverse on that image. The operator-centralizer image is precisely its displayed intersection; no density claim for that intersection is made. Arbitrary disk descent, transfer of a disk null-homotopy, and the general C12 filling remain unresolved.
